effort: Express a fast forward press from a settled start and control the finish.

explosive.name: Plyo Push-Up — paused bottom start, hands elevated
explosive.job: Primary fast push from a still loaded position rather than an immediate lowering-to-push rebound.
explosive.cue: On a stable elevated support, lower to a controlled bottom, hold 2 s without relaxing, then push into a small hand flight and soft return. Reset fully; no clap.
explosive.replacement: a fast non-flight incline push-up from the same controlled pause when hand reception is unsuitable; record zero hand landings
explosive.uniqueness_reason: Related to Class 1 E3 but removes the immediate eccentric-to-concentric reversal. The still loaded start is today's force problem; height or load changes alone are not counted as novelty.
explosive.key: Plyo Push-Up — paused bottom start, hands elevated

explosive.name: Band Triceps Pressdown — rapid elbow extension
explosive.job: Isolate quick elbow extension for the finish of the pressing action.
explosive.cue: Band on an inspected rated overhead attachment; elbows stay at ribs. Extend quickly without slamming lockout, return 2 s and keep shoulders still.
explosive.replacement: a very light floor-supported dumbbell elbow extension with decisive controlled ascent if the band anchor is unavailable
explosive.identity: Proposed exact execution; no verified canonical identifier
explosive.uniqueness_reason: First isolated rapid elbow-extension task; different from a full shoulder-and-elbow press. One small set supports the finish without another large pressing drill.
explosive.key: Band Triceps Pressdown — rapid elbow extension

explosive.name: Medicine Ball Catch-Set Chest Pass — gentle coach feed
explosive.job: Accept a small incoming load, stabilize it, then create forward force from a settled chest position.
explosive.cue: A coach gives a soft two-hand feed at chest height from a short inspected distance. Receive with yielding elbows, hold still 1 s, then pass forward; no immediate rebound chain. Use only a ball the athlete can comfortably receive.
explosive.replacement: a self-started stationary chest pass if feed control or receiving readiness is absent; record zero catches, and use a self-anchored band press if release containment also fails
explosive.identity: medicine-ball-chest-pass parent; coach-fed catch-set execution proposed
explosive.uniqueness_reason: First external load acceptance followed by a static release. A faster rebound pass was rejected because it adds reversal demand before receiving quality has been observed.
explosive.key: Medicine Ball Catch-Set Chest Pass — gentle coach feed

explosive.name: Floor Press — light dumbbells, fast concentric from floor contact
explosive.job: Accelerate an external load from a reproducible still start while the trunk is supported.
explosive.cue: Lower 2 s, settle upper arms gently for 1 s without losing tension, press quickly; keep grip throughout and decelerate before elbow lock.
explosive.replacement: a light self-anchored Band Chest Press if dumbbell handling cannot remain controlled
explosive.identity: Floor Press; migration 451; rapid light-load delivery proposed
explosive.uniqueness_reason: First rapid floor-press prescription; related to the existing primary lift and other presses, not a wholly new family. Open-chain acceleration differs from E1 moving the body off a support; only four light reps precede strength.
explosive.key: Floor Press — light dumbbells, fast concentric from floor contact

explosive.name: Band Chest Press — one arm presses while opposite arm holds
explosive.job: Create a forward pulse with one arm while the other maintains a steady press position.
explosive.cue: Self-anchored band across upper back, securely held; perform two pulses with one arm while the other stays comfortably extended during each pulse. Release both arms during resets; change working arm after the side rest. Keep ribs and shoulders facing forward.
explosive.replacement: a self-anchored single-arm band speed press with the nonworking hand securing the tail at the torso if the opposite-arm hold causes fatigue
explosive.uniqueness_reason: Introduces simultaneous steady and rapid arm roles rather than another bilateral press. Related to Class 2 band pressing; the hold must stay light and brief, with only two pulses per arm.
explosive.key: Band Chest Press — one arm presses while opposite arm holds

explosive.name: Two-Hand Landmine Bent-Over Row — fast pull from a pause
explosive.job: Retain one low-volume backward force task so the pressing day still includes deliberate pulling.
explosive.cue: Light load; still hinge, pull sleeve toward lower ribs quickly, lower 2 s, pause extended arms without hip drive.
explosive.replacement: a light two-hand kettlebell paused row if the landmine cannot be handled quickly
explosive.uniqueness_reason: Explicit Class 1 repeat at half its sets. A new rope-transfer or vertical-pull task would add grip/skill demands beside the first receiving task; three familiar arm-driven pulls preserve direct pulling with minimal added instruction.
explosive.key: Two-Hand Landmine Bent-Over Row — fast pull from a pause

resilience.name: Supine Dumbbell Serratus Reach — elbows straight
resilience.job: Lightly load scapular reach at the press finish while the floor supports trunk position.
resilience.cue: Very light paired dumbbells above chest; keep elbows straight, reach shoulder blades slightly off floor 2 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s without rolling the trunk.
resilience.replacement: an unloaded supine reach through the same comfortable range
resilience.identity: Proposed exact execution; no verified canonical identifier
resilience.key: Supine Dumbbell Serratus Reach — elbows straight

resilience.name: Bilateral Band External Rotation — elbows at sides
resilience.job: Light shoulder-rotator strengthening to control upper-arm position during the day's press and pull.
resilience.cue: Unanchored band between hands, elbows at ribs; rotate outward 2 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s without shrugging.
resilience.replacement: a lower-tension band and shorter comfortable range
resilience.key: Bilateral Band External Rotation — elbows at sides

primary.name: Floor Press — two dumbbells, neutral grip
primary.job: Main horizontal pressing force with a reproducible floor-limited range.
primary.cue: Lower 2 s, touch upper arms gently, pause 1 s, then press decisively; feet stay down. Coach supervises pickup/set-down.
primary.replacement: a lighter floor press through controlled comfortable range

primary.name: One-Arm Row — dumbbell, hand and knee on bench
primary.job: Load the arm-driven backward draw while support prevents torso rotation.
primary.cue: Draw elbow toward hip, hold 1 s, lower 2 s; stop before the shoulder rolls forward or the trunk turns.
primary.replacement: a thigh-supported dumbbell row with the same arm path if a bench does not fit

primary.name: Push-Up — controlled full repetition
primary.job: Second major press: load force from the bottom while shoulder blades move freely and the trunk remains fixed.
primary.cue: Lower 2 s, push decisively, finish tall through shoulders for 1 s; no hand flight. Adjust leverage or band resistance to reach 2–3 RIR.
primary.replacement: a hands-elevated push-up on an inspected immovable support

primary.name: Dumbbell Rear-Delt Row — bilateral, hinged
primary.job: Strengthen the wider-elbow backward draw that controls the arm-open position.
primary.cue: Hold a still hinge; elbows about 60 degrees from torso, pull to upper ribs, hold 1 s, lower 2 s.
primary.replacement: a chest-supported version only on an inspected bench with adequate arm clearance

primary.name: Dumbbell Skull Crusher — floor-supported
primary.job: Load elbow extension for the finish of a forceful press.
primary.cue: Neutral grips, upper arms near vertical; lower 2 s beside the ears, extend under control without shoulder swing.
primary.replacement: a lighter floor-supported elbow extension through comfortable range

primary.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl — simultaneous arms
primary.job: Load elbow flexors for finishing the backward draw without another shoulder-extension set.
primary.cue: Upper arms stay at ribs; lift 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s, without hip swing or wrist collapse.
primary.replacement: a lighter neutral-grip curl without body movement

progression: Class 3 emphasized pulling with Floor Press 1 × 6 and two main pulling lifts. Here Floor Press returns to its already prescribed Class 1/2 dose of 2 × 6, One-Arm Row drops to 1 × 6 per arm, and controlled Push-Up receives 2 × 6 instead of Class 2's 1 × 8. Eight primary rounds are retained, with 60 task reps rather than Class 3's 66. This is focus-based redistribution, not an earned increase. Hold loads at demonstrated 2–3 RIR; the added receiving/hand-flight demands can require same-slot regression or stopped work. Next progression needs actual controlled completion and recovery.
audit_findings: Main hand flights capped at six; all other pressing supports have four or fewer reps except the three gentle catch-set releases. Only three catches are prescribed, with a non-catching replacement if readiness is unconfirmed. The light speed floor press and challenging primary floor press are separately performed with different jobs/loads and are not double-counted. The later controlled push-up is not hand-flight work. Two new tasks, three related variants and one explicit repeat are recorded; no claim of six new movement families.
next_job: Class 5 should explore a small preload into a straight-ahead release, using receiving or reversal demands only when actual first-attempt control permits them. Review Class 4 hand/wrist and pressing exposure before selecting it.
